target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `write` tool always overwrites files completely. When multiple isolated sessions (e.g., main session + cron jobs) write to the same shared file, the last write wins and **prior content is silently destroyed** with no warning, no backup, and no recovery path. This is especially dangerous with cron/isolated sessions, where sub-agents independently decide to "log results" to a shared file and overwrite hours of main-session work.

Prompt-level guards are insufficient — sub-agents ignore or forget "NEVER overwrite" / "APPEND ONLY" instructions under complex task prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `write` tool provides no append primitive. To append, an agent must:
1. Read the full file
2. Concatenate new content
3. Write the entire result back

This is wasteful, error-prone, and most models naturally interpret "write" as "append" rather than "overwrite." Adding a first-class `append: true` parameter resolves the root cause — agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

Internal primitives already exist: `fs.appendFile` for host paths, `root.append()` for workspace-scoped paths in `@openclaw/fs-safe`. This change exposes them through the model-facing tool API.

## User Impact

- **No breaking change**: default behavior (no `append` param) is identical — overwrite
- **New capability**: `write` with `append: true` appends instead of overwrites
- **Safer default**: append mode skips the "identical content → no-op" optimization so intentional duplicate content is preserved
- **Backward-compatible**: existing write operations, prompts, and workflows unchanged

## Evidence

### Unit tests (12/12 passing)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

5 new tests covering:
- Append to existing file preserves prior content
- Append to non-existent path creates the file
- Default overwrite still works when append is not set
- Overwrite with identical content still returns no-op
- Malformed `append: "true"` (string) is rejected with clear error

### Live proof

```
Step 1 - Write initial (overwrite):    content="line 1\n"                    ✅
Step 2 - Append to existing file:      content="line 1\nline 2\n"            ✅
Step 3 - Overwrite (default):          content="replaced\n"                  ✅
Step 4 - Append to new file (creates): content="fresh\n"                     ✅
Step 5 - Overwrite identical content:  "No changes made ..."                 ✅
```

### Scope

**4 files changed**, 0 unrelated changes:
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — core schema/execute/recovery
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — WriteToolInput type
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — appendFile for sandbox/host/workspace paths
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new append-mode tests

Closes #40001


## P2 fixes (post-review)

### Sandbox byte preservation

The sandbox append path was a UTF-8 read-modify-write (`existing + content`); files containing invalid UTF-8 bytes had those bytes replaced with U+FFFD during append. Adds `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` that opens the pinned file with `O_APPEND | O_CREAT` via the same Python helper that backs `writeFile`, mirroring host `fs.appendFile` and `@openclaw/fs-safe` `root.append` semantics. Binary files (build artifacts, NDJSON chunks, image data) keep their original bytes through the sandbox path.

- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts` — `appendFile` impl on `SandboxFsBridgeImpl`, mirrors `writeFile` exactly (Buffer|string normalization, path-safety guard, pinned entry).
- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-mutation-helper.ts` — `APPEND_FLAGS = O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND`, `write_append(parent_fd, basename, stdin_buffer)` Python helper (opens, fstat checks, writes stdin chunks, fsync), `'append'` dispatcher branch, `buildPinnedAppendPlan` JS builder.
- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.types.ts` — interface declaration.
- `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts` — `appendFile` impl on `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge`.
- `extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts` — `appendFile` impl on `OpenShellFsBridge` (uses `@openclaw/fs-safe` `root.append`).
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:941-961` — `appendFile` collapses to a one-liner `bridge.appendFile({ ... mkdir: true })`.

### Post-mutation abort check

The if/else unification in the append branch silently dropped the `if (signal?.aborted) throw` that current main retains after `await ops.writeFile(...)` (sibling reference: `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts:460-463`). Restore the check between the append/overwrite branch and the success return so cancellation-after-success flows through `recoverSuccessfulWrite` (which now has append-aware content checks via `isRecoveredAppendContent`).

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts:484-507` — `if (signal?.aborted) throw new Error("Operation aborted")` inserted between the if/else (append|write) and the success return, applies to both branches.

### Tests

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — new tests `recovers success when appendFile aborts AFTER successfully appending` and `propagates abort when no successful append happened`. The first proves append-after-success recovery returns "Successfully appended"; the second proves abort-without-success does NOT manufacture a success.
- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts` — new `appends via O_APPEND (no temp file, no os.replace)` asserts `write_append(` is in the script, the dispatched operation is `append` (argv[1] == "append"), and the args include the target mount root + parent + basename.
- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts` — new pinned case `append pins canonical parent + basename` exercises `appendFile` through the canonical entrypoint.
- `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.boundary.test.ts` — new `blocks appends into read-only bind mounts` mirrors the existing `writeFile` boundary rejection.

### Sandbox contract surface

`SandboxFsBridge` is now `appendFile`-complete across `SandboxFsBridgeImpl`, `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge`, `OpenShellFsBridge`, and the host-sandbox test stub. Test fixtures that declare inline `SandboxFsBridge` literals (`agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts`, `apply-patch.test.ts`) gain matching `appendFile` entries to satisfy the contract.

## Verification

Local fallback (Crabbox unavailable in this env), per CLAUDE.md "report local fallback":

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts \
    src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.boundary.test.ts \
    src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts \
    src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts \
    src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
    src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  91 passed (91)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>
exit=0

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs
exit=0
```

target.title: fix(google-meet): actually leave the Meet call in the browser on leave (#103386)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103386.

`openclaw googlemeet leave <session-id>` on the Chrome transports printed `left <session-id>` and marked the session `ended`, but only ran the registered stop hook (the realtime audio bridge; in transcribe mode nothing at all). No code path touched the meeting, so the browser participant kept sitting in the call — a ghost participant receiving audio/captions after the operator was told it left. Twilio sessions already end the real call via their stop hook, so the transports were inconsistent.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/types.ts` + `chrome.ts`: join now persists the exact tab identity on the session — `browserTargetId` plus `browserTabOpenedByPlugin` (opened via `/tabs/open` vs adopted via `reuseExistingTab`). `openMeetWithBrowserRequest` returns it through both the local and node launch paths.
- `chrome.ts`: new `leaveChromeMeet` / `leaveChromeMeetOnNode` (shared `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest` core). Leave acts on the persisted target only: verifies the tab still exists (already-closed is a clean no-op), clicks Meet's **Leave call** button via browser evaluate (reliable now that tabs are pinned to `?hl=en`), then closes the tab **only when the plugin opened it** — reused user-owned tabs get the click but stay open. Failures degrade to session notes instead of throwing.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: `leave()` calls the browser leave for `chrome`/`chrome-node` sessions and records the outcome in session notes. Guards:
  - sessions with no tracked tab (e.g. `chrome.launch: false`, or browser control never returned a targetId) get an explicit note instead of a guessy URL match;
  - the internal tab-reassignment path in `join()` passes `keepBrowserTab: true` so agent handoff keeps the in-call tab and avoids lobby re-admission;
  - the shared-tab guard compares the persisted `browserTargetId` + node context — same meeting URL in a different browser/node no longer suppresses departure.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: `leave` row now documents the Chrome-transport behavior.

### Review follow-up (b95168f8ece)

All three ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed: leave no longer rediscovers tabs by URL (persisted `targetId` from join), never closes tabs it did not open (opened-vs-reused ownership tracked), and the shared-tab guard is scoped to the actual target + browser context. A reused-tab regression test now covers the default `reuseExistingTab: true` path end to end.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 209 tests passed. New/updated regressions: plugin-opened tab leave (click + close on the exact persisted target), reused user-owned tab leave (click, `DELETE` throws in the mock if attempted, tab stays open), already-closed tab leave (clean note, no `DELETE`), and a vm test that the leave script clicks only an enabled Leave call button.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- oxfmt / oxlint on touched files — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `googlemeet leave` leaves the browser participant in the Google Meet call on chrome/chrome-node transports while reporting `left`.
Real environment tested: No live Google Meet call was run; behavior is proven at the browser-proxy request boundary with the plugin's existing stubbed-gateway test harness (same harness the join/status paths use), covering opened, reused, and already-closed tab lifecycles.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` and `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts`.
Evidence after fix: "leaves the Meet call in the browser when a chrome session leaves" asserts the `/act` evaluate carries the leave-click script against the persisted join target and that `DELETE /tabs/local-meet-tab` is issued; "keeps a reused Meet tab open on leave" asserts the same click against an adopted pre-existing tab with a mock that throws on any `DELETE`.
Observed result after fix: 209/209 tests pass; leave issues real browser actions scoped to the session's own tab and records an explanatory note in every fallback path.
What was not tested: A live Meet meeting (real Chrome, real Google account) and the chrome-node transport against a physical node; both share `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest`, which is covered by the harness. Live-call proof of actual participant departure is pending a real Meet setup.
